accounts.name: auto_vote_enrollment
docs: Whether this exists (owned by this program) is what determines the
AUTO_VOTE_FEE_BPS split applies -- checked as raw account state in the
handler rather than trusting a client-declared flag, since "not
enrolled" must not be something a caller can simply assert to dodge
the fee.

accounts.name: bribe_token
docs: Per-token pause switch. May be an empty, system-owned account for a token
that was never configured (claims then stay open); the handler checks it
is the canonical PDA for `token_mint`.

accounts.name: user_token_account
docs: Created on first claim, so a voter who never held the bribe token can still claim it.

accounts.name: treasury_token_account
docs: Only ever written to when auto_vote_enrollment is populated -- created
lazily since most claims are never for an enrolled lock.

accounts.name: auto_vote_enrollment
docs: See the identical comment in claim_bribe_reward.rs.

accounts.name: treasury_token_account_a
docs: Only ever written to when auto_vote_enrollment is populated -- created
lazily since most claims are never for an enrolled lock.

accounts.name: caller
docs: Anyone (review H-2): only a change the Admin scheduled can run, and only once its epoch has begun.

accounts.name: enrollment
docs: Must have been made by the lock's current owner (review M-1).

accounts.name: auto_voter
docs: The voter must still be registered.

accounts.name: stake
docs: are checked before decoding. The saved owner and position never change.

accounts.name: caller
docs: Anyone (review H-2): the protocol PDA is the DEX's protocol-fee collector, and the fees can only go
into this epoch's vault for this gauge's voters.

accounts.name: epoch
docs: The epoch the fees are routed into. Fees routed into an epoch where the gauge has no votes could never be
claimed (DEV-10), so routing is refused until the gauge has votes; until then they stay owed in the pool.

accounts.name: occupant
docs: The gauge currently holding the pair, when there is one and it is not
this gauge. Its status decides whether the pair is free.

accounts.name: enrollment
docs: The lock must be enrolled in auto-vote: the choice only says who votes it.

accounts.name: authority
docs: The Admin, or the price keeper named in KeeperConfig (checked in the handler).

instructions.name: unlock_lock
docs: Unreachable on permanent locks: it requires `lock.is_expired()`, which
is always false. Superseded by `exit_lock`, which charges the published
exit fee instead of waiting for an expiry that never arrives.

accounts.name: caller
docs: Intentionally permissionless: anyone may crank the epoch forward once the
week boundary passes. The signer only pays the new `Epoch` PDA's rent;
no privilege is derived from being the caller.

accounts.name: auto_vote_enrollment
docs: Only required when `user` is the AUTO_VOTE_KEEPER voting on someone
else's behalf. The owner voting directly passes None.

accounts.name: allocation_voter
docs: Only required when `user` is the protocol Admin voting a registered
protocol allocation.

accounts.name: destination_token_account
docs: The Treasury's token account (DEV-15: the fee is protocol revenue, like exit fees, never the Admin's own).

types.name: AdminConfig
docs: Pause switches plus the pending side of a two-step Admin transfer. The
current Admin is `Protocol.admin`; there is no compiled-in admin list after
`initialize`.

fields.name: gate_phi_set
docs: Activity-gate threshold set by Admin; `gate_phi_ppm` only counts when
`gate_phi_set`, otherwise the DEX default applies. 0 disables the gate.

fields.name: treasury
docs: Where bribes for gauges that end up with no voters or were removed go.
`Pubkey::default()` until Admin sets it.

types.name: AllocationVoter
docs: Marks a lock as a protocol allocation (Treasury, Team, Advisors, ...) whose
votes the Admin casts (rule A10). `owner` is the wallet that held the lock
at registration: if the lock is later transferred, Admin voting lapses.

fields.name: votes
docs: Standing split (percent per gauge) the public crank applies each epoch.

fields.name: version
docs: Bumped on every Admin change to `votes`.

fields.name: applied_epoch_plus_one
docs: Epoch + 1 of the last application (0 = never), and the version applied.

types.name: AutoVoteDelegate
docs: A lock owner's choice of registered auto-voter for an enrolled lock. While it exists (and is newer than the
lock's current enrollment), only that voter may auto-vote the lock and the Solve3 keeper is refused. Closing
it (clear_auto_voter) hands the lock back to the Solve3 keeper.

types.name: AutoVoteEnrollment
docs: Marks a lock as enrolled in the public Auto-Vote program. Presence of
this account (at its canonical PDA, seeded by the lock) is what
authorizes AUTO_VOTE_KEEPER to cast votes on the lock's behalf (see
instructions/vote.rs) and is what charges AUTO_VOTE_FEE_BPS on the
lock's voting rewards to the protocol treasury instead of paying them
out in full (see claim_bribe_reward.rs / claim_pool_reward.rs).
A separate PDA rather than a Lock field for the same reason ExitConfig
is separate from Protocol -- Lock is already deployed at a fixed size,
so growing it would break every instruction that deserializes it.

types.name: AutoVoter
docs: A wallet registered to cast votes for enrolled locks whose owners choose it (DEV-12). Anyone may register;
registering gives no power by itself -- a lock owner must pick this voter with set_auto_voter. The auto-vote
fee is unchanged: AUTO_VOTE_FEE_BPS of an enrolled lock's voting rewards goes to the protocol whichever
voter casts its votes.

types.name: BribeToken
docs: Admin-managed policy for one bribe reward token (Full Launch rule A12).
`allowed` gates NEW deposits only. Delisting a token (allowed = false)
never touches obligations already created: claims keep working. `paused`
is the per-token emergency switch: it blocks new deposits and claims of
this one token without freezing any other reward.

fields.name: claimed_a
docs: Each side is claimed on its own, so a token that cannot be paid out
(for example a frozen destination account) never blocks the other.

types.name: ExitConfig
docs: The SOLV3 price the exit fee is charged against.
This is a separate account rather than a field on `Protocol` on purpose:
the deployed Protocol account was allocated at `8 + Protocol::INIT_SPACE`,
so growing that struct would make every instruction that touches it fail
to deserialize, and a migration couldn't load the account to repair it.
The rate is administrator-published, not an oracle reading. SOLV3 has no
price feed and its pools carry no liquidity, so there is nothing on-chain
to derive a market price from.

fields.name: lamports_per_solv3
docs: Lamports per whole SOLV3 (not per base unit).

types.name: ExitFeeConfig
docs: The exit fee percentage. A separate account from `ExitConfig` so the
price account keeps its layout. An account that was never created means
the initial `EXIT_FEE_BPS` applies.
Admin changes never apply to the current epoch: `set_exit_fee_bps` records
the new value for the next epoch, and `effective_bps` switches over once
the protocol reaches it.

fields.name: pending_epoch
docs: First epoch the pending value applies to; 0 = nothing pending.

fields.name: current_bps
docs: The percentage in force now.

fields.name: new_bps
docs: The percentage that applies from `effective_epoch`.

fields.name: is_active
docs: True while the gauge routes fees and streams emissions: ACTIVE and
PENDING_REMOVAL. Set only by `configure_native_gauge`.

fields.name: effective_epoch
docs: First epoch the pending change applies to (0 when none is pending).

fields.name: generation
docs: How many times this pool's gauge has been (re)listed.

types.name: GaugeScheduled
docs: kind: 0 = activation scheduled, 1 = removal requested, 2 = migration scheduled.

types.name: GaugeStatusChanged
docs: Emitted when a scheduled change is executed. status uses the GAUGE_* values.

types.name: KeeperConfig
docs: Narrow operational role the Admin assigns (review H-2): the price keeper may nudge the exit price within
the per-update bounds and nothing else. Everything else the keeper does is permissionless.

fields.name: amount
docs: SOLV3 base units returned to the owner — the full principal.

fields.name: fee_lamports
docs: SOL paid to the protocol treasury for the exit.

fields.name: lamports_per_solv3
docs: The rate the fee was priced at, for auditability.

fields.name: fee_bps
docs: The fee percentage (basis points) in force for this exit.

fields.name: remaining_amount
docs: SOLV3 base units still locked after this exit (0 for a full exit).

types.name: NativeGauge
docs: Versioned separately from GaugeReward: legacy liabilities stay in the old
vault and can never earn a second share of the new native LP stream.

types.name: PairCanonical
docs: The one gauge-eligible pool of a token pair (INV-G1). The PDA is derived
from the sorted pair, so two pools of the same pair always meet here.
`gauge` is the current or pending occupant; it is free again once that
gauge is REMOVED.

types.name: PartnerVoter
docs: Admin-flagged partner voter. A lock voted by this wallet pays no AUTO_VOTE_FEE_BPS when it claims; every other
auto-voter (including the Solve3 keeper) still charges the standard fee. A separate PDA keyed by the voter's
wallet, so no existing account layout changes.

types.name: PoolFeeVault
docs: Holds a pool's share of swept protocol trading fees for LPs to claim
directly, for pools that don't (yet) have a Gauge. Once a Gauge exists,
new fee sweeps are expected to go through distribute_pool_reward instead
-- this vault isn't disabled automatically (nothing here reads Gauge
state), it simply stops receiving new funding once an admin/keeper
switches which instruction they call. Existing balances here stay
claimable either way.

types.name: SolveRewardInfo
docs: Stores the state relevant for tracking liquidity mining rewards at the `Solve` level.
These values are used in conjunction with `PositionRewardInfo`, `Tick.reward_growths_outside`,
and `Solve.reward_last_updated_timestamp` to determine how many rewards are earned by open
positions.

fields.name: mint
docs: Reward token mint.

fields.name: vault
docs: Reward vault token account.

fields.name: authority
docs: Authority account that has permission to initialize the reward and set emissions.

fields.name: emissions_per_second_x64
docs: Q64.64 number that indicates how many tokens per second are earned per unit of liquidity.

fields.name: growth_global_x64
docs: Q64.64 number that tracks the total tokens earned per unit of liquidity since the reward
emissions were turned on.

fields.name: trading_pauses
docs: Trading pause switches (bit 0: swaps, bit 1: new liquidity). Occupies what used to be
padding, so the account size is unchanged.

types.name: TreasuryChange
docs: A Treasury change waiting for its delay (review H-1). `set_treasury` writes it; anyone can apply it once
`executable_at` has passed; the Admin can cancel it before then.

types.name: UpgradeSchedule
docs: A program upgrade waiting out its timelock. One per target program; closed
when the upgrade is executed or cancelled.

fields.name: rewards
docs: Emission rewards deposited via `distribute_reward` for this epoch/gauge.

types.name: VoteLockRecord
docs: Which lock produced a vote. UserVote is keyed by (lock, epoch), so each
lock has its own vote and one lock's vote never replaces another's. The
claim instructions still take this record, and check it against the lock
they were given, so the auto-vote fee can only be avoided by claiming with
the very lock that voted (which is the lock the fee is looked up on).
